our_title: Target weight conversion overflows to INT_MIN for arbitrary weights, then double-frees
ran: kits rebuilt per tree into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G25-metis-graph-part/repro/bin_<tree>/ (gcc -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -DSCOTCH_METIS_VERSION=5 ... -lscotchmetisv5; ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0); bin_asan/cli08 6 1: '0.185404 -> -2147483648' (x6), 'ERROR: archCmpltwArchBuild2: invalid parameters (2)', 'AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free'; 64-bit '0.185404 -> -55411773953759104' then the same. Patched (0001+0002): 'part 3: target 0.1812 actual 0.1812' ..., no report.
severity_note: review says medium; raised because in 7.0.17 the failure path double-frees the caller's array (PS2-G25-1), so arbitrary tpwgts (computed fractions are the common case) corrupt the heap instead of merely failing
review_accuracy: accurate on mechanism. Its Fix line 'round(w * 1e6), minimum 1' would turn a zero target into 1 and change the integer ratios of exact inputs (0.5/0.5 -> 500000/500000); 'cap doubadj' is right but the cap must be tested before the gcd: the intermediate doubtmp = doubadj / fraction reaches 1e12 before the lcm is formed, so a cap applied after the gcd still performs an out-of-range (int) conversion.
first_pass_critique: evidence right (INT_MIN values reproduced). Its tested diff clamps every weight to >= 1 (its own text says to drop that) and caps only after intGcd ((int) round (doubtmp)) with the possibly-overflowing cast, so the UB it set out to remove remains at the step that blows up; DOUBADJMAX = 1e4 is too coarse (targets below 1e-4 round to 0 and are then rejected by archCmpltw); it named the float twin but did not patch it; it did not notice the double free that its own repro printed.

extra_instances.location: src/libscotch/arch_cmpltw.c:184 (new defect PS2-G25-1, reached by this one)

fix_options.label: a: always round at a fixed resolution (drop the common-denominator search)
fix_options.summary: intetab[i] = round (doubtab[i] * 1e6) in both converters; intGcd no longer used there.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Simplest and always in range, but exact ratios change (0.25/0.75 gives 250000/750000 instead of 1/3) so archCmpltw weights and partitions differ from 7.0.17 for every weighted call; the ParMETIS 'skip equal values' optimisation becomes moot.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He wrote the gcd search to keep small exact integers; dropping it changes results for all existing users.

fix_options.label: b: bound the factor at 1e6, tested before the gcd (patch 0002)
fix_options.summary: doubtmp = doubadj / fraction; if doubtmp <= DOUBADJMAX reduce by the gcd; if the result exceeds DOUBADJMAX, set doubadj = DOUBADJMAX and stop (fixed resolution); casts become (SCOTCH_Num). Same in the float twin (FLOTADJMAX).
fix_options.tested: cli08 6 1 / 3 2 32/64-bit, check_libmetis_v5 and check_libparmetis_v3 with a new 9-weight array without small common denominator (pristine fails on both)
fix_options.tradeoffs: Exact small ratios preserved; arbitrary weights rounded at 1e-6 (sum of integer weights about 1e6, far below Gnum range; kgraph uses doubles for comploadavg).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Keeps his algorithm and adds a bound, as c5baef9 'Set tighter boundary on hypercube dimension' and 6a552f9 'Check overflow in intLoad()' do.

test_added: src/check/test_libmetis.c and test_libparmetis.c: bwgttab (9 six-decimal weights summing to 1) passed as tpwgts; checkPart. Pristine: archCmpltw error + double free.
